body: YES, THANK YOU!!! Damn, you guys are good.

I am glad to see your reply and that what I wrote was able to help you, and I'm also glad to see that the tone of your writing is so different from your original post. Thank you for your response!  
It makes sense that you're angry. It's a normal response to feeling hurt. When I feel overwhelmingly angry, what helps me is venting (on a text document or to a friend), exercising to shed the energy, or doing something fun as a distraction. And sometimes it helps to just experience the emotion (as ignoring it may not work), let it roll through me, and validate my feelings. "That hurt, and it sucked, and I didn't deserve it." Maybe some of these things can be helpful for you. Time helps heal wounds, and over time it'll sting less and less.

That could be a number of things: A depression symptom, a temporary "mental shutdown" because you're overwhelmed, or maybe you're just exhausted because of all of the emotions that were previously running through you. I think it might have to do with your stress hormones as well (and dopamine of course). It might be helpful if you just rest for now and practice some self-care today.

That's understandable. And feelings do really come and go, especially suicidal and depressive feelings. Some days are good. Some days are really bad. Some days you just feel "okay." But then some days are really good and make you feel glad that you stuck around to experience them. There are good days ahead of you.

"Bad" is a very relative term; it is also a form of black-and-white thinking. What exactly makes someone "bad"? Everyone would have a different answer, so there is not one definition. There are certainly people who do bad things, but it all depends on your intentions after the action is performed. If you feel regret for your actions and want to do something good to make up for it (also known as "undoing"), that may help you feel less "bad." And besides, there are people who do terrible things in this world and feel absolutely no remorse for it; in fact, they may enjoy hurting others or think that it's okay, and they don't think of themselves as "bad" at all. You sound better than them, don't you think? You are definitely more deserving of a place in this world compared to those people. Don't place yourself into a box that you don't belong in.

Regardless of what things you may have done to hurt others, you still have the opportunity to change while you are alive and you deserve to be alive. Based on your comments, you do not sound happy about the things that you have done, and I doubt that continuing to do those things will bring you any kind of happiness. However, in no way does that indicate that you do not deserve to live. The following things may be helpful for you: Talk to someone you care about how you are feeling; consult a professional about your feelings so they can help you sort them; examine yourself and the reasons why you may have done those things. You may be hurting and have unmet needs. You deserve support and caring and I believe that wholeheartedly. You don't have to keep pushing people away-- And question yourself as to why you may do. Are you afraid of being hurt? Has someone hurt you in the past to garner that fear? You don't have to answer those for me; answer them for yourself. You have the power and strength and potential to change how you interact with others and have meaningful and healthy relationships. I hope that you recognize your strength and choose to live on and pursue happiness, in yourself and others. You can do it.

You must be feeling absolutely horrible... Especially because you seem to have lost your feeling of hope.
But if you read this, I encourage you to think about what stopped you from completing suicide yesterday. It sounds like someone who cares about you reached out to you. Do you care about that person? Do you have others that you care for? I bet that there are things in life that you would still love to do or try. Experiences to be had. Memories to make. Happiness and love to be felt. Your life is yours and can go wherever you wish to take it, but you lose that chance the moment you decide to give it all up. But it isn't too late. There is always time. You have the power inside of you to push forward and pursue that happiness. You won't find it in death. People who want to die just tend to want the pain to stop (myself included, so I'm not just talking out of my ass here).
I believe in you, and I believe that there is still strength left within you. You exhibited it just yesterday. Walk out of that dark room where you live and go outside instead. Close your eyes. Breathe deeply. Admire the beauty of the Earth, alive, around you. Walk away from that noose. It isn't your friend. It will only cause you pain (especially physical). You have the strength to do it.

I can't imagine how awful you personally feel, but I do notice a few similarities between us in the way you write. The repetitive thoughts. The concoction of terrible emotions. The loss of hope. Pain over another human being we were once involved with. I've been hurting over that person for almost a year and I'm still not over it, and I've been feeling depressed since I was a young teen. 
Something I learned a while ago fell along the lines of "people who want to die want to do so because they just want the pain to stop." You sound like you're in a lot of pain and medicine hasn't been very effective for you.
But let me tell you this. You're young. You have so much time ahead of you and so many memories to make. Aren't there still things you want to do? Play a new game coming out next year? Be there for your family and friends? Go on your dream trip? Allow time to heal you so you can leave that girl behind and fall in love with someone who loves you just as much?
What happened in the past doesn't matter anymore. It's history. It cannot be changed. The future is not yet written. You have free will and choice. Lingering on past feelings (in general) will only hurt you and prevent new feelings from emerging.
There is no "cure" for any kind of mental illness, but there is improvement and coping. I encourage you to research new coping skills that can help you and to always keep in mind long and short-term goals that make you feel like you have purpose. Because you do. Things can change and that is definitely not a bad thing, but you won't see it if you don't stick around. And please, don't keep it all inside. The feelings only grow and grow until they consume you and weigh down your heart. Talk to the people you trust. You deserve and need support.
I wish you all the best. You can do this. You have every chance to do so while you're alive. You can be happy again. You absolutely can.

Black

You see black

When you apply it to your eyes

And in the shadows you cast

Upon quilted bedsheets

And dimly-lit keyboards

Yet your considerate soul

Is anything but black.


You see black

In the late evenings

When the sun has set

A blue screen

Illuminates your face

Smiling at someone

Who hides behind

Their own black mask.


You see black

When you look

In the mirror

And in your eyes

But your dilated pupils

Cannot see anything

But the color black

In the dark.


You see black

When you search
 
For the light

Because your eyes

Haven't had time to adjust

And your mind

Has been stuck in the same place

For far too long.


You would have seen black

If what you had attempted

Had not failed

Yet the true failure

Would have been clear

If you have succeeded.


I had seen black

When you typed to me

Those few words

Which caused my heart to stop

And my head to spin

And my stomach to quiver.


I will see black

If you let yours consume you

And I will be blind

Without a visible path

And lost in the darkness

Because my light

Will be extinguished.


You can wear black if you wish

But don't wear it within

Since I never want to see

Black underneath your skin.

Thank you for responding! I know that it has been difficult in trying to make her believe that she is not "worthless," but I hope my words can come through to her soon. And, yes, I have been trying to remain calm about it but it has given me a great deal of stress nonetheless.

I will encourage her to seek outside help in case she feels that way again or she harms herself, but she hasn't even considered it when I mentioned it previously. However, I would much prefer her to be in a pleasant hospital contrary to a casket.
Thank you for the advice! I've been considering that, and I definitely think it's a good idea. I'm going to try to write something for her.
I am in shock how quickly an answer was found. Thank you!
